title: make install JSON=1 summary and JSONL=1 progress records of nvidia-gb10-freebsd
description: Every record of the install contract that names schema_version 2.1 is one of two shapes: the progress record (kind: progress) and the summary record (kind: summary; the whole JSON=1 object, or the last row of a JSONL=1 run). A consumer dispatches on schema_version and, inside it, on kind. The summary record says what happened: next steps only for an installed install; a blocked install names its blocker and its fix and has no next steps; an interrupted install names how to resume it.

next.description: The next steps of a good install, one command per entry, each one fit to paste. Never prose: an explanation belongs in note. Only an installed install has next steps. A staged install (DESTDIR) has none: the files are only staged, so there is no step to run on this system. A blocked install has none either: it names its blocker and that blocker's fix instead. An interrupted install has none: it names how to resume it in resume.

resume.description: How to resume an interrupted install: one command, fit to paste. Present only for the interrupted outcome; a blocked install resumes by following its blocker's fix, and an installed install has nothing to resume.

requires_root_shell.description: The indexes in next that need a root shell: this user has no doas, sudo or su, so those commands are printed bare. Empty when the commands carry the root tool, or need no root.

note.description: English prose about the next steps: the boot-load note (it names the command make configure YES=1), the line that says which steps run as root, and, for a staged install, where the files are. It may name a command; the commands to run are in next.
